text: {"claims":[{"claim_text":"A shared cache may reuse a cached response to a request with an Authorization header whenever the response is fresh.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passage says a shared cache MUST NOT use such a cached response unless a Cache-Control response directive allows it to be stored by a shared cache; freshness alone is not sufficient.","citations":[{"index":0,"quote":"A shared cache MUST NOT use a cached response to a request with an Authorization header field (Section 11.6.2 of [HTTP]) to satisfy any subsequent request unless the response contains a Cache-Control field with a response directive (Section 5.2.2) that allows it to be stored by a shared cache, and the cache conforms to the requirements of that directive for that response."}]},{"claim_text":"When a stored response is served without validation, the cache must generate an Age header equal to the response's current_age.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage requires generating an Age header with a value equal to the stored response's current_age when a stored response is used without validation.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"When a stored response is used to satisfy a request without validation, a cache MUST generate an Age header field (Section 5.1), replacing any present in the response with a value equal to the stored response's current_age; see Section 4.2.3."}]},{"claim_text":"If several suitable responses are stored, the cache must use the oldest one.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passage states the cache MUST use the most recent one, not the oldest one.","citations":[{"index":2,"quote":"When more than one suitable response is stored, a cache MUST use the most recent one (as determined by the Date header field)."}]},{"claim_text":"A cache may serve a stale response whenever it is disconnected, even if the response carries must-revalidate.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passages prohibit generating stale responses when must-revalidate applies and require an error response when disconnected rather than reusing the stale response.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"A cache MUST NOT generate a stale response if it is prohibited by an explicit in-protocol directive (e.g., by a no-cache response directive, a must-revalidate response directive, or an applicable s-maxage or proxy-revalidate response directive; see Section 5.2.2)."},{"index":7,"quote":"in particular, if a cache is disconnected, the cache MUST generate an error response rather than reuse the stale response."}]},{"claim_text":"When it cannot revalidate such a response it should return 502 (Bad Gateway).","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passage says the generated status code SHOULD be 504 (Gateway Timeout) unless another error status code is more applicable, not 502.","citations":[{"index":7,"quote":"The generated status code SHOULD be 504 (Gateway Timeout) unless another error status code is more applicable."}]},{"claim_text":"A cache must invalidate the target URI after a non-error response to an unsafe method.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage requires invalidating the target URI when a non-error status code is received in response to an unsafe request method.","citations":[{"index":4,"quote":"A cache MUST invalidate the target URI (Section 7.1 of [HTTP]) when it receives a non-error status code in response to an unsafe request method (including methods whose safety is unknown)."}]},{"claim_text":"A cache may also invalidate URIs from the Location header even when their origin differs.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passage says a cache MUST NOT trigger invalidation if the origin of the URI to be invalidated differs from that of the target URI.","citations":[{"index":5,"quote":"However, a cache MUST NOT trigger an invalidation under these conditions if the origin (Section 4.3.1 of [HTTP]) of the URI to be invalidated differs from that of the target URI (Section 7.1 of [HTTP])."}]},{"claim_text":"The no-store request directive only applies to shared caches.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"The passage states that the no-store request directive applies to both private and shared caches.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"This directive applies to both private and shared caches."}]},{"claim_text":"The unqualified private directive forbids shared caches from storing the response but lets a private cache store it.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"The passage states that a shared cache MUST NOT store the response and that a private cache MAY store it, subject to constraints.","citations":[{"index":8,"quote":"The unqualified private response directive indicates that a shared cache MUST NOT store the response (i.e., the response is intended for a single user). It also indicates that a private cache MAY store the response, subject to the constraints defined in Section 3, even if the response would not otherwise be heuristically cacheable by a private cache."}]}]}
